script: Punjabi (Gurmukhi), Shree-Lipi 7 family. Composers: S8PunU64.dll (Unicode) and S8Pun764.dll (raw 7 bytes). They answer for Punjabi, even though Shree's Converter does not. The pipeline was adapted from tsk-ban, with a new probe2.exe. probe2 checks after every LoadKbdOverlay that table 0 of SL8_DLL_DATA equals the keyboard file (#loaded). It loads from 8.3 short paths, uses neutral probe names (PAAA.PUN …) and builds on a copy of ITR.PUN (k/BASEA.PUN). I first checked that the composers were sound by re-capturing ITR.BAN; it was byte-identical to the 11 Oct capture (capcheck/). SLNXT state: SL8_DLL_DATA was all zero before my run, meaning no keyboard had been loaded since SLNXT started at 00:59. I restored it by writing the saved dump back (probe2 --put) and verified it identical three times; it is all zero now. A test showed a probe load changes only SL8_DLL_DATA. SL8_DEFAULTS_DATA did change 2 bytes during the session (0x90 01->00, 0x92 20->00), but not because of my loads, so I left it alone. Builds: probe2 and measure, one at a time, with UseSharedCompilation=false. No UI, typing, clipboard or Word was used.

coverage:
pun7-groundtruth.json has the same shape as ban7: about, composers, counts, truth, pairs. It holds 59,839 rows ({unicode, bytes, source, kind}), 31,436 Unicode strings, and 27,752 strings with truth {preferred, accepted, alternatives}; 1,272 rows are quirks.

Sources:
- 12 vendor keyboards, 1,576 script rows. CRTRONIC DOE ENG GODREJ INSCRIPT ITR NEWROMA PHONETIC RAMING ROMA TYPEWRIT VARITYPE.PUN, loaded from their original paths because the composers switch to a phonetic mode by name (ENG/NEWROMA/PHONETIC/ROMA).
- 58,349 probe sequences in 1,242 probe keyboards: P 36,941, H 19,968, S 1,440.
- Exploration sets: E 521 and F 106.

What the probes cover:
- Every one of the 32 consonants and 6 nukta letters (ਸ਼ ਖ਼ ਗ਼ ਜ਼ ਫ਼ ਲ਼): alone, pending link, halant, link+ZWJ/ZWNJ, +nukta.
- Each letter with the 4 subjoined codes (D1 ੍ਰ, D2 ੍ਹ, D0 ੍ਵ, 4C ੍ਯ), the 4 tails (ਂ ੰ ਃ ੱ), all 12 tail pairs, and all 9 vowel signs (ਿ struck first) alone, with each tail, and with the legacy-only codes 41/EE.
- Subjoined forms with every sign, tail and sign+tail, plus pending link/halant.
- All 32x32 two-consonant clusters through the link code 64 AND through the halant code 44, each alone, with every sign, tail and subjoined form, and with a pending link/halant.
- Nukta letters inside clusters.
- Independent vowels and carriers (ਅ ੲ ੳ ਓ, E4) with tails.
- Every single code 21-FE except the slot references.
- Lone signs.
- The 52 unique vendor conjunct-slot sequences.
- 128 word probes (ਕਿ+C, ਕਿੱ+C, ਪੱ+C+ਾ, ਕੀ+C). All 128 equal the concatenation of their syllables.
- The other typing orders ("every typing order"; Gurmukhi has no reph): ਿ struck after the letter, a sign struck before the subjoined code, a mark before the sign, link/halant + ਰ ਹ ਵ ਯ, and all 6 orders of ਠ/ਨ/ਕ + subjoined + sign + tail. These are kept as alt:*.
- Three-consonant clusters that fit in 4 codes: C੍C + ੍ਰ/੍ਹ/੍ਵ/੍ਯ (for example ਸ੍ਤ੍ਰ).

Not covered:
- Anything over 4 codes, because a slot holds at most 4: ਿ + C੍C + tail; C੍C + subjoined + sign; a nukta letter in a cluster with a sign; C੍C੍C where the third letter has no subjoined form.
- Udaat ੑ (U+0A51) and yakash ੵ (U+0A75). No code 21-FE and no vendor key produces them.
- The Ctrl+Shift+1 symbol layer. The tutor cannot reach it: layers 2-12 all return the raw code table (layers/ITR-L12.tsv). It is taken from the charts instead, the same in all 13 Punjabi charts: $=₹ (code EF -> 3C), *=× (DC -> 23), /=÷ (DD -> 24). These are in pun-vendor-keys.json, section ctrlShift1.

Codes only the 7 composer types (the Unicode composer gives nothing):
- 41 -> 40, an avagraha-like ऽ glyph.
- EE -> A9, a short low dash.

Codes the 7 composer types nothing for: 64 (link), D7 (nukta, except the 6 nukta letters, which have their own glyphs), E2/E3 (ZWJ/ZWNJ), E4 (ਇ), E0 (ੴ), 7C “, 7E ”, D9 ॥.

There are 83 composer gaps, listed in pun7-composer-gaps.json. These are Unicode strings where the 7 composer loses a glyph, so they have no truth:
- ਠ/ਨ + subjoined + ਾ/ੁ/ੂ + ਂ/ੰ/ੱ. Example: ਨ੍ਹਾਂ (as in ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ and ਜਿਨ੍ਹਾਂ) comes out as B2 BE A3 BE AA, with no 70 and BE written twice.
- Two subjoined codes in a row: ਕ੍ਹ੍ਰ = 48 6E.
- ਠ/ਨ + subjoined + a top sign + bindi: ਠ੍ਰੇਂ = 53 79 BE 7A.

For 36 of the 83, the composer's own rules give one spelling. For example ਨ੍ਹਾਂ -> B2 BE AA 70 A3, which I render-checked in fonts/check3.png.
stability:
Every capture was run twice in separate probe processes, and both runs were byte-identical:
- 12/12 vendor keyboards (capvo vs capvo-b).
- 786/786 P files, 425/425 H files and 31/31 S files.

Inside each run, probe2 asks every key twice. All files have #stable 1 and #loaded 1: table 0 of SL8_DLL_DATA matched the keyboard file after each load, so no load failed and no other process interfered.

In probeparse, the untouched ITR check keys V X Z : ; 0 5 agreed on all 1,242 probe files (W and Y are slot keys in ITR and cannot serve as checks).

The composers matched the 11 Oct Bangla capture byte for byte, even though SLNXT's SL8_VFC* blocks are now empty.

Quirks found:
- No "Lk"/"Hf" placeholders in Punjabi.
- No answer is given to many keys at once.
- Unicode carriers: a leading space on lone signs (13,919 answers) and a '.' before the i-sign (1,270). 44 answers end in NUL (the ਇ answer is 0A07 0000).
- The 7 composer returns -256 ("nothing") in 3,791 answers. 18 phonetic-keyboard answers sit on carrier byte 07, which no font has.

Name-driven modes:
- ENG, PHONETIC, NEWROMA and ROMA answer consonants with C + ੍ (134 vendor rows marked quirk), and their bindi key types tippi (A5).

Unicode composer rules (accepted):
- A tippi typed after ਾ ੀ ੇ ੈ ੋ ੌ ਉ ਊ ੳ is written as bindi U+0A02, in 1,015 rows. The 7 bytes match the bindi probes.
- ੱ then ਂ is written as ਁ U+0A01, in 49 rows.
- ੳ + ੋ stays ੳੋ; it does not become ਓ.
- ੴ is U+0A74 for both 51 and 31 51.

Unicode composer quirks (954 rows): ਡ + nukta -> ੜ; ਓ + ੁ -> ਉ; with the late-ਿ order it moves the i-sign while the 7 composer loses the subjoined code.

7 composer quirks:
- Loses the addak after ੀ/ੇ/ੈ/ੌ + ਂ (6 rows).
- Loses a vowel sign or subjoined glyph on ਠ/ਨ (55 + 50 rows).
- Drops “ ” ॥ ੴ(E0) ਇ(E4).

Layer alignment:
- For Punjabi, unlike Bangla, both composers answer layer 1 and the raw-code layer by the code the key holds (layercheck: L1 124/124 agree, L2 570/584). The 14 misses are the phonetic modes. All layers are therefore used.
family:
One table can serve both families. The only exception is ₹.

Fonts compared (fontcmp.js; I wrote a TTF reader that renders by glyph index, which avoids the 0xAD trap):
- 7: WPUN7001.TTF (SHREE-PUN7-0951) and WPUN7002.TTF (SHREE-PUN7-0952). Each has a (3,1) format-4 cmap with 119 codes and 123 glyphs.
- 4/5/6: S09500F2, S09510F2, S09520F2, S09550F2 and S09560F2.TTF (SHREE-PUN-0950/0951/0952/0955/0956). Each has 118 codes and 122 glyphs.

Results:
- Same-design pairs (0951: WPUN7001 vs S09510F2; 0952: WPUN7002 vs S09520F2) match on 118 of 119 codes, with identical glyf bytes and advances. The one difference is 3C (₹), which only the two 7 faces have.
- All five 4/5/6 faces map the same 118 codes to the same glyph ids. Both 7 faces map the same 119 codes to the same glyph ids.
- Every byte the 7 composer writes into the truth exists in every face, except 3C, which is missing from 4/5/6 (bytesInTruthNotInAnyFont = []).
- Missing from all faces: 07 (the phonetic carrier) and 78/7B/80-9F/C0+.
- languages.json already wires all 7 Punjabi faces to shree-pun7. That is correct, apart from ₹: for a 4/5/6 face it must be dropped or reported.

Glyphs identified from the renders (fonts/codes-*.png, check1-3.png):
- B0 is the onkar arc without the ੧. Code 51 alone writes B0; the complete ੴ is 31 B0 (VARITYPE key O).
- A8 is the addak placed further right, used after top marks. A7 is the addak over the letter.
- A4 is the bindi to the right of ਉ/ਊ. 44 is ੳ + bindi.
- 73 7A 7C 7E A2 are the sign+bindi ligatures for ੀ ੇ ੈ ੋ ੌ.
- BE is a spacer, advance 120, written after ਠ (53) and ਨ (B2).
- AE/AF are ੁ/ੂ for use after BE.
- 6E is the ਕ੍ਰ ligature. 6F, AA, AB and 62 are the subjoined ੍ਰ ੍ਹ ੍ਵ ੍ਯ.
- B5 is the halant.
currentTables:
Tables measured: unicode-to-shree-pun7.json (238 pairs, 1 preRule) and shree-pun7-to-unicode.json (93 pairs), run through the real FontConverter built from my snapshot copy (repo/src/FontSoftware.Core, repo/assets/config). These are identical to the main checkout's tables.

Forward (Unicode to bytes):
- Exact: 25,260/27,752 = 91.02%.
- Accepted: 25,260/27,752 = 91.02%. Whenever the table is right it writes the preferred spelling. Our table writes the visible halant B5 for C੍C, which matches the preferred choice.
- 2,492 strings fail; 7 of those match a Shree alternative.
- 141 rows report unmapped characters: ਁ 46, ZWJ 38, ZWNJ 38, ₹ 1, plus 18 ASCII characters that pass through correctly.
- The same strings in NFC form (nukta letters decomposed): 1,086/1,146 = 94.8%.
- 20,000 random joined words: 75.58% exact. No pair or rule reaches across a syllable; every word failure comes from a syllable that fails on its own.
- Common Punjabi words: 198/238 exact (83.2%). Wrong ones include ਨੂੰ ਨੇ ਇੱਕ ਇਹ ਇਸ ਉੱਤੇ ਉੱਚਾ ਉੱਥੇ ਇੱਥੇ ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਜਿਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਤੁਹਾਨੂੰ ਸਾਨੂੰ ਮੈਨੂੰ ਨੌਂ ਨੰਬਰ ਬਠਿੰਡਾ ਠੰਡ ਕੈਨੇਡਾ ਇੰਗਲੈਂਡ ੴ ₹ (measured/common-words.txt).

The tables' own round trip (Unicode to ours and back to Unicode) is 27,751/27,752 = 100.00%. That is the "tests pass" figure, against 91% byte-exact.

Reverse (Shree's preferred bytes to Unicode):
- Exact: 26,627/27,752 = 95.95%.
- Same text: 26,718 = 96.27%.
- All accepted spellings, same text up to the virama the link spelling cannot show: 43,782/47,157 = 92.84%.
- 874 rows read unmapped bytes: BE 695, AF 81, AE 80, 3C 1.

Forward failure categories (Unicode: ours | Shree):
1. Addak after a top mark must be A8, not A7: 887 strings. ਉੱ 45 A7 | 45 A8 (affects ਉੱਤੇ ਉੱਚਾ); ਕੀੱ 48 72 A7 | 48 72 A8; ਕਂੱ 48 A3 A7 | 48 A3 A8.
2. Spacer BE after ਠ/ਨ: about 1,100 strings.
   - BE missing before a subjoined form: 428. ਨ੍ਹ B2 AA | B2 BE AA; ਠ੍ਰ 53 6F | 53 BE 6F.
   - Top marks written after BE instead of before it: 546. ਨੇ B2 BE 79 | B2 79 BE; ਨੂੰ B2 BE 76 A5 | B2 A5 BE 76; ਨੰ B2 BE A5 | B2 A5 BE; ਠੱ 53 BE A7 | 53 A7 BE; ਨੌਂ B2 BE A2 | B2 A2 BE.
   - ੁ ੂ after BE must be AE AF: 136. ਨੁ B2 BE 74 | B2 BE AE; ਨੂ B2 BE 76 | B2 BE AF.
   - ਠ/ਨ + subjoined + sign: for example ਠ੍ਰੇ 53 6F 79 | 53 79 BE 6F.
3. i-sign not moved in front of ੜ, the nukta letters U+0A59-0A5E, ੲ, ਅ, ੳ or ਓ: about 86 strings. The preRule only covers U+0A15-0A39. ਇ 42 71 | 71 42 (affects ਇਹ ਇਸ ਇੱਕ); ਖ਼ਿ 69 71 | 71 69; ੜਿ 6D 71 | 71 6D; ੜ੍ਹਿ 6D B5 71 68 | 71 6D AA.
4. ZWJ/ZWNJ passed through: 76 strings. ਕ੍‍ 48 B5 U+200D | 48; ਕ੍‌ 48 B5 U+200C | 48 B5.
5. ਁ U+0A01 unmapped: 43 strings. ਕਁ 48 U+0A01 | 48 A7 A3.
6. Bindi ligatures on independent vowels: about 20 strings. ਈਂ 42 72 A3 | 42 73; ਏਂ 42 79 A3 | 42 7A; ਐਂ 41 B1 A3 | 41 7C; ਔਂ 41 A1 A3 | 41 A2; ਊਂ 46 A3 | 46 A4; ੳਂ 43 A3 | 44.
7. ੴ B0 | 31 B0.
8. ₹ U+20B9 | 3C (7 faces only).

Reverse failure categories:
1. A standalone BE, AE or AF is read as ¾, ® or ¯ (856 strings). B2 79 BE gives ਨੇ¾; B2 A5 BE 76 (ਨੂੰ as Shree types it) gives ਨੰ¾ੂ; B2 BE AE gives ਨ®.
2. 71 before ੜ or a nukta letter is not reordered (about 90). 71 6D gives ਿੜ, should be ੜਿ.
3. 48 A7 A3 reads ਕੱਂ; the Unicode composer writes ਕਁ (44 strings).
4. 31 B0 reads ੧ੴ; should be ੴ.
5. 3C reads '<'; should be ₹.
6. 44 reads ੳ; should be ੳਂ.
keyboards:
All 12 shipped Punjabi keyboards are captured key by key from their original paths (C:\Shree-Lipi nxt\*.PUN), in both composers (U and 7), twice in separate processes (byte-identical), each run asked twice. MODULAR exists only as a chart and has no .PUN file.

Layers captured:
- Layer 0, the printed keyboard (normal and shift are separate ASCII keys): 1,031 answered keys.
- Layer 1, Ctrl+Space: 151.
- Layer 2, the composer's raw code layer (key character = internal code; layers 3-12 answer the same): 1,004.

Per keyboard (layer 0/1/2): CRTRONIC 87/16/83, DOE 77/21/83, ENG 81/12/87, GODREJ 81/18/83, INSCRIPT 89/6/83, ITR 92/12/83, NEWROMA 82/13/83, PHONETIC 81/12/87, RAMING 89/8/83, ROMA 85/16/83, TYPEWRIT 93/10/83, VARITYPE 94/7/83.

Where the data is:
- Raw captures: capvo\*.tsv (run A) and capvo-b\*.tsv (run B), one per keyboard.
- Compiled: pun-vendor-keys.json. For every key it gives the internal codes the key holds (conjunct slot expanded, in typed order), the raw Unicode answer in hex, the cleaned Unicode, and the 7 bytes.
- The Ctrl+Shift+1 symbol layer cannot be reached through the tutor. Its section (ctrlShift1) comes from the charts: $ ₹ = EF -> 3C, * × = DC -> 23, / ÷ = DD -> 24.

Notes for a later per-key audit:
- ITR/DOE/CRTRONIC/GODREJ/RAMING/ROMA Ctrl+Space q, and other keys holding code 51, type ੴ as B0, the arc without the ੧. VARITYPE key O types 31 B0.
- RAMING key P (codes 31 42 4D) types ੧ੳ = 31 43.
- Phonetic keyboards (ENG, NEWROMA, PHONETIC, ROMA) answer consonants as C੍, the bindi key as tippi A5, and lone signs on byte 07.
notes:
What still blocks a perfect table:

(1) Shree's own 7 composer has no usable answer for 83 strings (pun7-composer-gaps.json). Among them is ਨ੍ਹਾਂ, which is in very common words (ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ, ਜਿਨ੍ਹਾਂ, ਇਨ੍ਹਾਂ). 36 of the 83 have a rule-derived spelling; the 47 with ੁ/ੂ + tail on ਠ/ਨ + subjoined have none.

(2) Policy choices the composer cannot settle:
- Virama before a letter with no subjoined form. The link code writes no glyph (ਕ੍ਤ = 48 57, the same bytes as ਕਤ). The halant code writes B5 (48 B5 57). The truth prefers B5, accepts both, and the current table writes B5.
- ੴ: 31 B0 (preferred) against B0 (what 11 vendor keys type).
- ॥ “ ” have no 7 spelling at all; candidates are 26 26 and 22 22 / 27 27 (the ShreeNonIndic look-alike policy).
- ਁ (U+0A01) against ੱ + ਂ.
- ₹ exists in the 7 faces only.

(3) The table must take nukta letters both precomposed (as the Unicode composer writes them) and in NFC (letter + U+0A3C).

(4) Codes 41 -> 40 (avagraha-like) and EE -> A9 (low dash) have no Unicode identity from the composer.

(5) Clusters longer than 4 codes cannot be probed.

Fix priorities, by how often the words occur:
- BE ordering and the AE/AF variants for ਠ/ਨ. ਨੂੰ, ਨੇ, ਨੌ and many others fail in both directions; reverse prints ¾, ® or ¯ into any Shree document with ਨ/ਠ + mark.
- A8 after ਉ (ਉੱਤੇ) and after the top signs.
- The i-sign reorder for ੲ/ੜ/nukta letters, which breaks ਇ.
- Drop ZWJ/ZWNJ.
- Add ਁ, ੴ and ₹.

The TypingEngine was not measured in this run (the task asked only for the FontConverter). pun-vendor-keys.json is ready for that audit.

Memory note candidates:
- The Punjabi tutor has no Ctrl+Shift+1 layer; tutor layers 2 and up are the raw code table. For Punjabi both composers answer Ctrl+Space and the raw-code layer aligned.
- SLNXT's SL8_DLL_DATA can be all zero when no keyboard has been loaded. Restoring it means writing the saved dump back, because LoadKbdOverlay cannot produce zeros.
